name: @destaworks/admin
//: WHY THIS MANIFEST EXISTS, when apps/web has none.
apps/web is built by the ROOT package (`app:build`: `next build apps/web`) and inherits the
root manifest. That is migration residue, not a pattern: web WAS the root application until
Phase 2.9 moved its files under apps/, and the manifest stayed where it was.
Two checks in scripts/check-architecture.mjs are gated on `hasOwnManifest` and are skipped
entirely for a unit without one: `imports <workspace package> but the manifest does not
declare it`, and `imports external <package> undeclared in its manifest`. Inheriting the root
manifest would opt admin out of both on its first day, and would silently hand it every
dependency the root app declares -- including @destaworks/db, @destaworks/application and
@prisma/client, which are exactly what admin must never reach. The manifest is where
`admin is HTTP-only` stops being a comment and becomes a fact a tool reads.
The cost is real and accepted: every external and every workspace package admin imports has
to be declared here, and adding one is a visible diff rather than an inherited accident.
//scripts: Deliberately none. The console is built by the ROOT package (`admin:build`:
`next build apps/admin`), like apps/web, because the working directory decides what Tailwind
v4 scans: from apps/admin it would root there and never see the classes inside
@destaworks/ui. One build path, run from the repo root, is the whole reason.
